query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy used as a thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation during sliding in the intended high-temperature operating regime? Define a controlled change relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the corresponding directional changes in wear and deformation, state the regime in which those predictions should hold, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The wear resistance and microscopic deformation of a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy coating on a conventional metal substrate during sliding in the high-temperature operating regime are governed by the coating's grain size and the resulting grain boundary sliding mechanism.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy coating with an average grain size of 10 μm
generation.intervention: Controlled change in grain size to 1 μm through annealing at 900°C for 1 hour
generation.conditions: Sliding wear test at 500°C with a normal load of 10 N and a sliding speed of 0.1 m/s
generation.mechanism: Grain boundary sliding and dislocation glide
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% decrease in wear rate and a 25% decrease in microscopic deformation relative to the baseline coating condition
generation.baseline: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy coating with an average grain size of 10 μm
generation.boundary: Grain size range of 1-10 μm and temperature range of 400-600°C
generation.uncertainty: The actual wear resistance and microscopic deformation may be influenced by other factors such as coating thickness, substrate material, and testing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Sliding wear test with varying grain sizes and temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear rate and microscopic deformation do not decrease by at least 20% when the grain size is reduced to 1 μm, the hypothesis is falsified
